open.options: Scoped byte-width access and sharing enums; named create/truncate/exclusive/native booleans replace positional integers. The file service still owns path validation, native/stream selection, sharing and resource admission.
open.result: Transient result holds a signed 16-bit token (or -1) and missing flag. The registry owns every accepted token; errno remains the failure detail. Returned structs never enter saved records.
open.mode_boundary: MdOpenFlags retains its explicit unsigned 16-bit ABI/layout. StreamOpen decodes access, sharing, create/truncate and no-error policy once at the game/platform boundary. Lower stream-mode parsing, exclusive creation, native identity and session token reuse/destruction retain their behavior.

The same assertions use named options/results afterward. Existing Unicode/missing/malformed-path, exception, session cleanup and file-service contract checks remain; invalid typed access still rejects before mutation.

byte_and_seek.result_contract: A present count, including zero, reports transferred bytes; nullopt reports a failed operation through errno. Positive partial counts and persistent stream error/EOF state remain separately observable. No all-or-nothing write promise is added.
byte_and_seek.capacities: Real fixed arrays and their tails become byte spans; the SDK preserves null-pointer checks before forming views. Record-stream and raw element APIs still bridge their existing caller-supplied ranges pending physical-span migration.
byte_and_seek.provider: The actual COMPATFILEREADSCOPE provider and held-lock exception witness receive/return the same span/optional-count types. No old raw-pointer provider adapter remains. SDK _lread/_lwrite map optional results back to their unchanged native counts/LastError/EINTR contract.
byte_and_seek.seek_contract: Scoped NATIVESEEKORIGIN is carried through core, host, ZIP/library, metadata, SDK and test consumers. Integers exist only at the actual OS/SDK boundary; SDK invalid origins are rejected before conversion. The token helper retains its existing fallback-to-end behavior for a forced nonstandard origin. Existing 32/64-bit position and overflow rules remain.
byte_and_seek.layout: fileio.h gives transient standard-library/service values native packing and restores caller packing. The actual packed Win32 include fixture checks optional-count and native metadata alignment and packing restoration. No saved record uses these values.
byte_and_seek.reference_checks: Before migration the actual native/token functions passed byte/count/sentinel checks, explicit EOF observation, size queries preserving EOF, current/end/begin seeks, invalid native origins and POSIX empty-write effects. After migration the same checks use spans/results; the zero-write test also covers both native and buffered backends.
byte_and_seek.initial_test_corrections: A first reference assertion incorrectly expected every short native-descriptor read to set EOF; corrected it to perform a further read that returns zero at EOF, retaining prefix/sentinel checks. A Windows test initially used a buffered stream while expecting native truncation; expanded it to require native truncation and buffered ENOTSUP, preserving existing implementation behavior. A missed SDK pointer span extent was corrected before final compilation.
byte_and_seek.call_inventory_scope: 98 listed direct expressions across ten native/token byte/seek functions, plus the actual SDK read-provider invocation. Concrete file Read/Write/Seek member handoffs also use spans or the scoped origin.

policies.readWrite: Existing read/write file, without truncation; r+b.
policies.writeTruncate: Create or truncate, write only; wb/w.
policies.writeAppend: Create or append, write only; ab.
policies.writeExclusive: Create only if missing, write only; wbx.
policies.readWriteExclusive: Create only if missing, read/write; w+bx.

SDK prototypes and actual Windows CRT behavior are unchanged.
